transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-20
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE); Marcus Li (Redwood SE); Priya Nair (Redwood Solutions); Tom Reynolds (NimbusCompute); Sara Lim (Nimbus - SA); Diego Marquez (Nimbus - Cloud Ops); Lina Hu (Nimbus BD)

Summary:
Quick partner intro between Redwood and NimbusCompute to assess fit for integration (Nimbus as a GPU/cloud partner). Discussed deployment models (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC), networking/KMS needs, compatibility with Nimbus GPU SKUs, partner commercial model, and next steps for a technical deep dive and pilot.

Topics:
- Partner integration scope and business model
- Private deployments and VPC connectivity
- Hardware compatibility (NVLink, A100/H100, custom mezzanine cards)
- Security: SOC2, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO
- Pilot sizing and timelines

Action items (captured above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll give a quick run through of who we are at Redwood and then dive into what a partner integration with Nimbus might look like
[00:12] Tom (Nimbus): hey thanks Ava, excited to talk, we've been seeing a lot of customer demand to have an integrated inference offering, and we like the idea of pairing our GPU pool with Redwood's runtime
[00:24] Marcus (Redwood SE): cool, I'm Marcus, run infra and the runtime team, i'll focus on the technical constraints - network, driver stack, kernel level stuff, that sort of thing
[00:33] Sara (Nimbus): quick note, we have multiple SKUs, A100 and H100 based racks, some with nvlink backplane and some without, also a newer HGX variant, hope that's useful context
[00:45] Marcus (Redwood): perfect, that helps - for reference Redwood has hosted, dedicated and private modes; private means the control plane can be customer-managed, we support VPC peering, private link style connections, and on-prem air-gapped installs as well
[00:58] Diego (Nimbus): when you say private, is our networking handled by you or do we keep the traffic inside Nimbus? we're sensitive to cross-cloud egress especially for enterprise customers
[01:08] Ava (Redwood): good q, for partner private deployments we typically offer two patterns: 1) we run a private control plane and the inference nodes sit inside partner VPC with egress policies you control, or 2) full on-prem package where customer manages both data plane and control plane - in both cases we support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys
[01:26] Tom (Nimbus): okay good, KMS matters - we have HSMs and bring-your-own-key options for some customers; curious how Redwood integrates with those
[01:35] Marcus (Redwood): we have bindings for common KMS providers and an HSM shim for enterprise installs, personally i'll want to validate exact HSM models but we usually do envelope encryption and keep minimal key material on node
[01:47] Sara (Nimbus): are there any kernel or driver requirements - we run a custom NVIDIA driver build for our newest racks, and we want to avoid breaking that flow
[01:57] Marcus (Redwood): we try to be flexible, we support CUDA 11.x and 12.x families and have a small compatibility matrix; for custom builds we can run a validation matrix - that said some inference optimizations (e.g., fused kernels or certain Triton integrations) expect stock drivers, so there might be some tuning
[02:13] Lina (Nimbus): pricing and revenue split question - is this more of a marketplace referral or co-sell where Nimbus gets cut on infra consumed?
[02:22] Ava (Redwood): good high-level - a lot of this is partnership specific; common patterns we've done: managed marketplace (partner bills for infra and we bill for control plane/services), or a reseller model with commit discounts for Dedicated capacity. We'll share a one-pager after the call with typical commercial options
[02:38] Tom (Nimbus): sounds good. also curious about multi-tenancy - we have customers that need strict tenant isolation, can Redwood enforce per-tenant KV cache boundaries and RBAC?
[02:48] Marcus (Redwood): yes, we support tenant isolation at multiple levels - per-route/model tenancy, KV cache scoped per-tenant, RBAC integrated with SSO/SAML; audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM as well
[03:02] Sara (Nimbus): transcription note: (laughs) we're still using your public docs as reference, sometimes the product names get swapped, like Redwood Dedicated vs Redwood Private, so happy to get a doc that maps the terms
[03:12] Priya (Redwood): we'll include a mapping, and also a short matrix that shows which features are supported in each deployment mode
[03:20] Tom (Nimbus): on performance: we want to run a pilot for 3 models: a 8k instruction-following model, a chat model with streaming, and an embedding workload. expected SLOs: p95 < 200ms for streaming tokens on the chat model when pinned to dedicated GPUs - is that realistic?
[03:40] Marcus (Redwood): p95 <200ms depends heavily on batching, sequence length and KV cache hits; with dedicated H100 pools and optimized kernels we can often hit that, but we'd need to benchmark with your payloads. we should plan a perf run with representative prompts, and we can recommend quantization or batching settings to trade cost/latency
[03:56] Diego (Nimbus): bandwidth between host and GPU matters for kv-heavy ops, we have racks with nvlink across 8 GPUs, others are 4-GPU racks - would that change how you place replicas?
[04:08] Marcus (Redwood): yes, topology matters - the runtime picks kernel selection and memory placement based on NVLink topology; for multi-GPU sharded models we prefer NVLink-connected groups. we'll include a compatibility checklist in the follow up
[04:20] Ava (Redwood): another commercial/ops q - how do you handle burst capacity? if a customer needs short-term bursts above committed capacity, is there an option to spin on-demand nodes?
[04:30] Tom (Nimbus): yes we do allow burst via spare capacity pools, but pricing differs; we'd need to align on control-plane policies so the app can fallback gracefully if burst is constrained
[04:40] Priya (Redwood): we have routing policies that can send traffic to cheaper model variants or to hosted fallback endpoints; for partner scenarios we can coordinate a fallback order: local Nimbus nodes first, then Redwood hosted as fallback, or vice versa depending on contract
[04:56] Sara (Nimbus): on observability, customers want token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency dashboards, do you export traces/pass-through metrics?
[05:06] Marcus (Redwood): yes we emit per-request traces, tokenized cost breakdowns, and support OpenTelemetry hooks; logs can be shipped to your S3/ELK or GCP stack, and we support a retention policy per-customer
[05:17] Diego (Nimbus): compliance - SOC2 and ISO-type certifications our larger customers ask for, do you have those?
[05:24] Ava (Redwood): Redwood is SOC2 Type II certified and working through ISO currently; we'll send the certification summary and the security deck after this call
[05:33] Tom (Nimbus): perfect. one more thing - for joint go-to-market, we'd like a simple reference architecture and some co-branded collateral, can Redwood support that?
[05:42] Priya (Redwood): yes, we have partner enablement kits and a partner portal with co-brand templates; we'll include a link in the follow up
[05:49] Lina (Nimbus): timeline: if we want to run a pilot by end of Nov, what are the lead times?
[05:56] Marcus (Redwood): depends on whether it's Dedicated capacity or Private on Nimbus. For dedicated pools on Nimbus, provisioning can take 2-4 weeks once SKUs are agreed. On-prem/full private can be 6-8 weeks accounting for networking and HSM provisioning. We'll aim to calendar a technical deep-dive next week to lock down details
[06:12] Tom (Nimbus): ok let's do the deep-dive, ideally SE-led with a focus on the kernel stack and perf benchmarks
[06:19] Ava (Redwood): sounds good - next steps recap: 1) we'll send partner one-pager, SOC2 summary, and integration checklist; 2) Nimbus shares SKU list and perf targets; 3) schedule SE deep-dive week of Oct 4; 4) plan pilot sizing and pricing after deep-dive
[06:38] Diego (Nimbus): noted - i'll pull the SKU list and internal perf numbers, sara will coordinate
[06:44] Sara (Nimbus): yep I'll do that and set up the deep-dive invite once we have dates
[06:50] Ava (Redwood): awesome, thanks everyone, we'll follow up, and Marcus will take the tech lead for the deep-dive
[06:58] Marcus (Redwood): thanks all, bye

End of transcript
